lines.en: More than a dozen legs move as one.
My shell slides along the ground.
Not fast, and very quiet.
I slip past the edge of the stone.
Two antennae test the way.
Plains grass scrapes my back.
Every so often I pause.
My back is in segments.
I slip under a leaf.
I travel in a curve.
I have too many feet to count.
I follow a ridge of soil.
The sheen on my shell is faint.
I shift forward slowly.
I turn whenever I touch something.
I stop and consider.

lines.zh: 我贴着地面走，避开太阳
lines.en: I keep low to avoid the sun.

lines.zh: 我的壳边缘有一圈浅色
lines.en: A pale rim runs round my shell.
I curl into a half ball.
My legs are tucked under the shell.
I have found a cool spot in the soil.
I have gone entirely still.
There is a small crack in my shell.
Something crawled over my back.
I slowly uncurl.
This soil is soft and loose.
My antennae turned half round.
I am listening to a very faint sound.
The sun is on my shell.
I settle in comfortably.
My antennae come out first to test you.
You are above me, very large.
I can withdraw entirely into my shell.
You extend a finger.
I tap with an antenna, then retract.
My shell is very hard.
You have me wholly in your shadow.
Even balled up, I keep one slit open.
Your voice is a little loud.
I crawl slowly to your hand.
Your hand is warm.
I am not really a biter.
I curl up completely.
A fresh crack in my shell.
I have been flipped over.
My legs flail for a while.
I slowly right myself.
I pull every leg inside my shell.
The shell took most of it.
That kept me curled a long while.
The shell cracked, but my legs still move.
Do not flip me over.
The smell of the leaf is faint.
Leave it; I will come myself.
My mandibles are too small to gnaw it.

lines.zh: 我一条腿一条腿挪过去
lines.en: I move over one leg at a time.
There is a hint of sweetness.
I will curl up after this.
This leaf is a little dry.
Do you have a tender one?
I chew very slowly.
You should keep this yourself.
Dead leaves feed me for a day.
Lay the leaves out for me.
One touch and I curl up.
My shell hits the ground with a dull sound.
I peek out from the shell gap.
After a while I uncurl.
You stepped on my shell.
I roll another half turn.
That pushed me off course.
My legs are pinned under me.
I slowly right myself.
I move only after you walk off.

lines.zh: 我壳下有一片软的地方
lines.en: There is a soft place under my shell.
Curling up together is enough.
The soil is safer than the surface.
We have never made a fuss.
This ridge of soil will do for us.
Shift a little toward the damp soil, next to me.
Under the ridge we can lie side by side.
Two of us roll rounder together.
Close together, it is warm.
Let our shells touch first.
I hold it with many legs.
It is much heavier than I am.
Even all my legs cannot push it.
It is stuck at the edge of my shell.
I gnawed it; it's stone.
I shoulder it away with my shell.
I cannot carry it on my back.
I try to climb over it.
The weight makes my legs sag.
I have crawled past it.
The vibration reaches my belly plates.
First I curl up.
The shell is my best defence.
I wait it out.
I will move once you are gone.
I am beneath a blade of grass.
I am not at all afraid.
You cannot reach my soft parts.
I can still roll away.
I know this ground well.
I have curled tighter than before.
This shell serves me well.
I watch you through the shell gap.
You are still standing there.
I do not move; neither do you.
I press myself even lower.
My antennae are pulled in.
I make almost no sound.
Step on me and you will find me hard.
I can afford to wait.
The cool of the soil is good.
I tighten up and wait for you to misstep.
I count the times you press the soil.
I move only when you have gone.
I curl into a complete ball.
Kick me and I only roll.
My shell hits your foot.
That was me rolling into you.
There is nothing soft exposed.
I rolled down the slope.
A stone finally stopped me.
I slowly open up.
I am still dizzy.
I butt your foot with my back plate.
I turn up from under the leaf litter.
The leaf litter makes a fine hiding place for me.
First I tested my antennae.
The wind on the plains is strong.
I slowly extend my legs.
Companions crawl nearby.
My shell does not stand out in the grass.
I have found a leaf.
The sun is harsh; I head for shade.
I press my body to the cool soil.
Nothing dangerous here.
I begin to crawl forward.
My plates scorch, and I curl up tight.
My shell rolls to the bottom before it stops.
Water pours in through the shell gap.
The blast leaves me on my back.
Something strikes my shell loudly.
That force numbs my legs.
Hungry enough to chew dry leaves.

lines.zh: 雷打在附近，我缩得更紧
lines.en: Lightning strikes nearby and I curl tighter.
Nowhere here to tuck my legs.
